claim: matriliny raises female autonomy and lowers female childlessness but not quantum
evidence: matriliny lowers female childlessness (near-universal reproduction) yet Mosuo TFR is not high; co-resident female kin compete (Mattison matrilineal puzzle) - autonomy up, quantum flat

claim: paternity uncertainty is offset by avuncular (mother's-brother) investment
evidence: the avuncular buffer only partially compensates the dyadic-investment loss; net per-child investment is lower - a partial offset, not a wash

claim: matrilocal residence delivers grandmaternal childcare (a real cost-of-children lever)
evidence: the matrilocal add-on lifts the sweep materially (+matrilocal optimum dTFR +0.184) - but this is the kin-childcare channel (E26 H201), not the descent system

claim: stacking co-resident female kin pools childcare and raises fertility
evidence: same-sex kin crowding turns cooperative into competitive beyond a small optimum (Mattison 2011) - antagonistic, not additive

claim: matriarchy makes high-quality men exit, lowering retained male quality
evidence: tail selection on the male-q distribution: at s=0.5 the exit fraction is 0.64 and retained mean falls to -0.32 - the strong men withdraw first

claim: female hypergamy on the weak retained pool collapses coupling
evidence: with the desirability-gap bar b=+0.18, the coupling multiplier falls to 0.02 at s=0.6; the hypergamous match fails on the low-q remainder

claim: the instability needs no male aggression - pure withdrawal and selection suffice
evidence: the collapse is driven entirely by the exit tail-operation and the hypergamy bar; no coercion term is invoked - the structure is self-undermining

claim: the collapse threshold is predicted by a hypergamy bar calibrated from unrelated dating data
evidence: the dating-market desirability gap (Bruch-Newman) sets b=+0.18, which predicts a coupling-halving collapse at s*=0.38 - a cross-domain calibration transfer

claim: men are the infrastructure/defence substrate - their exit drops security S
evidence: the S withdrawal scales with the exit fraction (0.64 at s=0.6); the matriarchy depends on the male buy-in it erodes

claim: paternity severance lowers the next generation's marriageability a generation later
evidence: isolating the father-access channel (E30 intergenerational memory): near-zero contemporary effect (+0.000 at 2045) but -0.100 by 2095 - un-marriageable men and women downstream

claim: matriarchy compounds - it degrades the next generation, not just the present
evidence: the delayed alienation stacks on the immediate hypergamy coupling loss; the structure is worse over generations than in any single one

claim: avuncular investment buffers the intergenerational father-absence cost
evidence: raising the avuncular share reduces the fF severance and the delayed cost - a real but partial buffer, never a full substitute for dyadic investment

claim: the matriarchy collapse runs on two timescales - hypergamy now, alienation a generation later
evidence: the FULL matriarchy already craters coupling contemporaneously (-1.310 at 2045 via hypergamy), and the paternity channel adds a further delayed cost (-0.100 by 2095) - a double-timescale collapse, not a slow one

claim: state funding of the matriarchy repairs it
evidence: the state-funded variant optimum is s=0.10 dTFR=+0.782; the subsidy lifts S but cannot retain high-q men or satisfy hypergamy - it does not fix the instability

claim: media normalisation of matriarchy shifts the norm enough to stabilise it
evidence: a media N-push does not touch the exit or hypergamy mechanism; it is the E25 weak-pronatal-lever result again - cheap talk against a structural collapse

claim: engineering male retention stabilises the matriarchy
evidence: retaining high-q men requires restoring the status and paternity certainty that DEFINE the matriarchy's compression - a self-contradiction; you cannot have both

claim: there is an interior matriarchy strength that raises fertility
evidence: the pure-matriarchy sweep optimum is at s=0.00 with dTFR -0.008 - the optimum is the no-matriarchy corner; the exit-hypergamy instability dominates the interior

claim: the collapse is dominated by the exit x hypergamy interaction
evidence: in the interaction matrix the male-exit x paternity/coupling cell is +0.317; the buffers (avuncular, matrilocal) antagonise the losses - exit and hypergamy multiply into the collapse

claim: a stable pro-fertility matriarchy exists under the right conditions
evidence: it would need low hypergamy AND high male retention AND strong kin childcare - but retention is mutually exclusive with the paternity compression that defines matriarchy; no stable configuration in the developed regime

claim: the transferable part of matriarchy is matrilocal kin childcare, not the descent/paternity system
evidence: only the matrilocal-childcare add-on lifts fertility (+0.184); the descent + paternity-compression core is self-undermining via exit and hypergamy - keep the kin care, drop the structure
